OBJECTIVES
Nida Experiment Card PC130 - 255
Definition
In this lesson, you will use two different photomotion sensors to measure RPM and velocity of a moving object.
INTRODUCTIONM
The motion sensors used are the interrupter and reflector.i
In the first part of the experiment, you will measure RPM and velocity directly from a sensor.
Then you will measure RPM and velocity from a sensor circuit that uses a F/V chip.
In the optional second part of the experiment, you will use an oscilloscope and observe acceleration and deceleration.
Let's begin the lesson on MOTION TRANSDUCER OPERATION.....................

RPM AND VELOCITYTLE
In this experiment, you will observe the operation of motion sensors and measure the RPM and velocity.
EXPERIMENT
The motion sensors are mounted on the PC130-255 experiment card. Pick up the card and examine it.
The disk is rotated by a small DC motor, this produces motion.
On the disk are holes and dark areas that are used by the different motion sensors.
Locate PS1 on the card. This is the photoreflector sensor and is only on one side of the disk.
It uses the dark and silver areas on the disk to detect motion.
The dark areas WILL NOT reflect light, the silver areas WILL reflect light.
PS2 is the photointerrupter sensor. The light transmitter is on one side of the disk and the light receiver is on the other side.
It uses the holes and the absence of holes to detect motion.
Note that the schematic of the entire card may be viewed by selecting the schematic button anytime it is indicated on your screen.
The disk motor circuit consists of three switches that set up a DC output voltage to the motor through IC2 and IC3.
IC2 is a chip that changes digital inputs to analog. Switches S1 through S3 input digital data (000 to 111) and the output is a DC voltage on pin 8.
IC2 is a chip that changes digital inputs to analog. Switches S1 through S3 input digital data (000 to 111) and the output is a DC voltage on pin 8..
The output of IC2 is amplified by IC3 and applied to the motor.
As the switches are placed to IN, from 000 to 111, the motor will rotate the disk faster.
The output of the photointerrupter, PS2, does not use a F/V chip. The output is shaped by IC4 and sent to TP8.
